data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin word 'clemens', meaning mild, merciful, or gentle. This name is associated with Saint Clement, a 1st-century Christian martyr. The name Clementina carries the meaning “Mild, merciful, gentle” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Clementina usually hope their child will grow to embody mild, merciful, gentle and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Saint Clementina of Antioch, also known as Clementia, was a Christian martyr who lived in the late 2nd or early 3rd century. According to tradition, she was a slave girl purchased by her master Maximus, who was a Roman military officer. Maximus was converted to Christianity by Clementina's faith and her acts of charity towards other slaves and the poor. Clementina was martyred in Antioch during the persecutions of Emperor Maximinus Thrax in 311 AD.

Saint Clementina of Arezzo, also known as the Good Clementina, was a laywoman and a Franciscan Tertiary. Born in Arezzo, Italy, at the end of the 15th century, she was known for her deep faith, her charitable works, and her devotion to Saint Francis of Assisi. She was beatified by Pope Paul VI in 1963.
